title: Comparison of scalar affine input laws
statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be probability spaces, and let $X\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $Y\colon\Xi\to\mathbb R$ each satisfy the fourth-order invariance moment conditions: they are measurable up to null sets with finite fourth absolute moments, have means zero, second moments one, third moments zero, and fourth moments at most $9$. Let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be four times continuously differentiable, and suppose $C\ge0$ and $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for every real $t$. For all $a,b\in\mathbb R$,
\[\left|\mathbb E_\mu[\psi(a+bX)]-\mathbb E_\nu[\psi(a+bY)]\right|\le\frac{3C}{4}b^4.\]
hypotheses_covered: $X$ satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions under $\mu$.
$Y$ satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions under $\nu$.
$\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is four times continuously differentiable.
replaced: Let $X$ and $Y$ be real inputs on possibly different probability spaces, each measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. Let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $C^4$ and let $C\ge0$ satisfy $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for all real $t$. For every real $a,b$, $|\mathbb E\psi(a+bX)-\mathbb E\psi(a+bY)|\le(3C/4)b^4$.
